Because Emmalyn does not have depth, the antecedent of this rule, (writes XOR avoids), would be false either way (a false antecedent makes no trouble).  The usable information, however, is that whatever state that would give her depth is not the case; we do not yet know which of the two parts (writes or avoids) fails, but we do know this:
   
2. Emmalyn is not introspective ⟹ By the other exclusive-disjunction rule "avoids-publicity XOR values-privacy ⟹ introspective", the consequent is false, so the antecedent must be false.
3. Hence (avoids XOR values) is false, meaning avoids and values-privacy always take the same truth-value.
4. Emmalyn does not explore new ideas ⟹ By "reads-widely ⟹ explores-new-ideas", she therefore does not read-widely.
5. "writes-novels OR reads-widely ⟹ creative" ⟹ Because neither she reads-widely (from 4) nor thinks-deeply (explicit), she cannot produce art; to remain consistent with "(thinks OR creative) ⟹ produces-art", she is not creative either.
6. Thus she neither reads-widely nor is creative.  Because "writes-novels OR reads-widely ⟹ creative", for her not to be creative with certainty she must also not write-novels (otherwise even with ¬read she would be forced to be creative).
7. So we know: ¬write-novels, and (from 3) avoids ≡ values-privacy.  Combine with 1’s disjunction that writes-novels and avoids are the same (so that writes XOR avoids is false), we now have ¬avoids and thus ¬values-privacy.
8. Finally, "x is reclusive ⟹ x values-privacy".  Because Emmalyn does not value-privacy, modus tollens gives ¬reclusive.

The context therefore entails ‘Emmalyn is not reclusive.’
